title: Concatenated Words
summary: Given an array of unique strings, identify and return all words that are formed by concatenating at least two other words from the array.
statement: Given an array of unique strings, identify and return all words that are formed by concatenating at least two other words from the array.
constraints: 1 <= words.length <= 10,000; words are unique lowercase English strings of length 1..30; total characters <= 100,000.
Return all dictionary words formed from at least two strictly shorter dictionary words, in any order.
A shorter word may be reused. A word cannot count itself as a one-piece decomposition.
hints: Try decomposing each candidate using other, strictly shorter words.
Recursively solve the remaining suffix and memoize its starting index. Forbid the unsplit whole candidate.
For each end after start, check the dictionary slice and recurse on end; reaching the end means success.
A first cut guarantees at least two pieces. Reuse dictionary entries freely; memoization avoids repeating suffix failures.
editorial: Every legal decomposition chooses a first shorter prefix and then a decomposition of the remainder. Skipping the whole-word first edge prevents self-acceptance while leaving every multi-piece path. Memoized start positions bound repeated search. The oracle enumerates cut-position subsets rather than memoized suffixes. This returns qualifying dictionary words, unlike Word Break's boolean or sentence list.

tests.explanation: The results split as cats+dog+cats, dog+cats+dog, and rat+cat+dog+cat. Reusing a shorter word is allowed.
Only aaa qualifies: a+a+a uses three pieces. Neither single-letter word can be split.
